title: Operations Cost Manager

Fischbach USA focuses on reliable, precision-engineered packaging solutions that support efficient product delivery and application. Role Description The Operations Cost Manager is a full-time, on-site role based in Elizabethtown, KY, responsible for overseeing and optimizing production and operational costs across the organization. title: Director of Manufacturing

title: Quality Assurance Manager
job_description: About the role Gourmet Culinary Partners (GCP) makes handcrafted hors d’oeuvres, sides, breakfast offerings, and desserts for chefs and foodservice operators across the United States. At our GCP-Chicago location in Countryside, Illinois, you’ll lead the team responsible for food safety and quality from the moment ingredients arrive until finished foods are released. Reporting to GCP’s senior Quality Assurance leader, you’ll coach quality technicians and inspectors, lead the site’s food safety team, and serve as the primary site contact during audits and inspections. You’ll work directly with Production, Sanitation, R&D, and Supply Chain to resolve issues and help employees put food safety standards into practice on the production floor. What you’ll do Lead the site QA team. Hire, train, schedule, and develop quality technicians and inspectors. Set clear expectations and verify that required checks are completed and documented. Manage food safety plans. Serve as HACCP Team Leader and Preventive Controls Qualified Individual (PCQI). Lead hazard analysis and verify critical control points and preventive controls for processing, allergens, sanitation, and the supply chain. Lead audits and inspections. Maintain the site’s Safe Quality Food (SQF) system, conduct internal Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) inspections, and coordinate USDA, FDA, customer, and third-party audits. Document findings and verify that corrective actions are effective. Investigate food safety and quality concerns. Determine the root cause of process deviations, foreign material findings, out-of-specification results, and customer complaints. Contain affected food, escalate concerns, and work with site leaders to prevent recurrence. Oversee sampling and testing. Coordinate microbiological testing and environmental monitoring. Review results for trends, maintain laboratory equipment and calibration records, and use findings to guide sanitation and production decisions. Verify supplier, labeling, and traceability controls. Confirm that ingredients come from approved suppliers, review labels and Nutrition Facts panels with the labeling specialist, and maintain the site’s traceability and recall programs. Train employees and communicate findings. Update standard operating procedures, train employees on the production floor, and share audit findings, complaint trends, and quality metrics with site and corporate leaders. What you’ll bring Seven or more years of food industry experience managing food safety and quality technicians, preferably in a USDA- or FDA-inspected manufacturing facility. A bachelor’s degree in food science, food technology, microbiology, chemistry, quality assurance, or a related field, or equivalent food industry experience demonstrating the technical skills required for the role. HACCP and PCQI certifications. Working knowledge of USDA and FDA requirements, HACCP and HARPC food safety plans, current GMPs, sanitation programs, and allergen controls. Experience with third-party audits under a GFSI-recognized program, such as SQF or BRCGS, and the ability to fulfill the site’s SQF practitioner responsibilities. Training and hands-on experience in microbiological testing and environmental monitoring. The ability to coach employees, explain technical findings to production teams and auditors, and use Microsoft Office, including Excel, to analyze results and report trends. Work environment This position works on-site in an active food manufacturing facility with cold, wet, and hot production areas. Essential functions include standing for extended periods and lifting up to 20 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation. The annual base salary range is $85,000–$93,000, with a short-term incentive opportunity based on company performance. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, a 401(k) retirement savings plan, and paid time off. A detailed benefits overview is available upon request. title: Quality Area Manager
job_description: Summary The Quality Area Manager is responsible for leading food safety, quality, sanitation, and regulatory compliance programs within the CH food manufacturing plant while partnering closely with operations, maintenance, engineering, and supply chain teams to ensure safe, compliant, and high-quality product production. This role provides daily leadership and technical guidance to quality personnel, drives continuous improvement initiatives, leads root cause investigations, and supports the development of a strong food safety and quality culture across the plant. The Quality Area Manager serves as a key decision-maker during quality and food safety events, balancing risk assessment, regulatory requirements, operational needs, and customer expectations. Responsibilities include oversight of quality systems, verification activities, process monitoring programs, hold and release decisions, corrective and preventive actions, audit readiness, and compliance with company policies and regulatory standards including SQF and FDA requirements. Success in this role requires strong leadership, communication, technical problem-solving, and the ability to influence cross-functional teams in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Major Position Responsibilities It is an essential requirement of the job that the employee have the ability to function in a feedback-rich, team-based environment. Employees must possess good interpersonal skills and be compatible with co-workers. ESSENTIAL 40% TECHNICAL EXPERTISE Provides daily leadership and technical oversight of food safety, quality, sanitation, and regulatory programs. Maintains compliance with SQF, FDA, customer, and internal food safety and quality requirements. Leads quality and food safety investigations, including root cause analysis, risk assessment, containment, corrective actions, and preventive actions. Serves as a technical resource for process deviations, product disposition decisions, foreign material events, and consumer complaints. Verifies execution and effectiveness of prerequisite programs, process controls, sanitation activities, allergen controls, and documentation practices. Reviews quality data and operational trends to identify emerging risks and opportunities for improvement. Partners with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Supply Chain, and Corporate Quality teams to ensure processes remain controlled and compliant. Supports audit readiness and participates in internal, regulatory, and customer audits. Maintains a strong floor presence to verify standards, coach employees, and identify issues in real time. Ensures accurate documentation, record review, hold management, traceability, and disposition activities are completed appropriately and on time. 20% CONTINUOUS PROCESS IMPROVEMENT Drives continuous improvement initiatives focused on food safety, product quality, process capability, operational efficiency, and reduction of chronic losses. Uses data, trend analysis, and structured problem-solving tools to identify root causes and implement sustainable corrective actions. Facilitates cross-functional collaboration during investigations, process changes, trials, validations, and improvement projects. Identifies opportunities to simplify, standardize, and strengthen quality systems, work instructions, and operational practices. Supports development and implementation of new technologies, processes, equipment, and monitoring systems. Promotes proactive risk identification and prevention rather than reactive problem solving. Encourages a culture of learning, accountability, and continuous improvement across the plant. 40% LEADERSHIP Leads, coaches, and develops Quality team members to build technical capability, ownership, accountability, and leadership skills. Establishes clear expectations and provides timely feedback regarding performance, behaviors, and development opportunities. Builds strong cross-functional relationships and fosters collaboration between Quality, Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, and Supply Chain teams. Creates an environment where food safety and quality are treated as shared plant responsibilities. Supports staffing, scheduling, prioritization, and resource allocation to ensure effective daily execution. Leads by example through professionalism, urgency, communication, and visible commitment to food safety and employee engagement. Helps develop future leaders through mentoring, coaching, and delegation of meaningful responsibilities. Communicates effectively across all levels of the organization, from frontline employees to plant and corporate leadership. Maintains composure and sound decision-making during high-pressure situations, production challenges, and food safety events. Reinforces a culture of accountability, teamwork, respect, and continuous learning. SUPPLEMENTAL Fiscal Responsibility: Travel Expenses, Plant Quality Department Budget Internal Customers: Supply Chain: Plant Leadership/Administration, Plant Operations, Plant Engineering, Receiving, Shipping, Planning External Customers: RD&I: Technical Services, Sensory and Consumer Science, Product Development, External Affairs and Consumer Response

title: Quality Manager
job_description: Company Description For over 60 years, McLean has been the proven, one-stop source for innovative, high-impact packaging solutions. title: Controller
job_description: Job Title: Controller Department: Finance & Accounting Reports To: President / Chief Executive Officer / CFO Employment Type: Full-Time Position Summary The Controller is responsible for overseeing the organization's accounting operations, financial reporting, budgeting, internal controls, and financial compliance. Essential Duties and Responsibilities 1. Financial Management & Reporting Oversee all daily accounting operations, including accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll, and general ledger. Prepare and review monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements. Ensure accurate and timely financial reporting. Provide recommendations to improve profitability and control expenses. 3. Internal Controls & Compliance Establish and maintain effective internal financial controls. Maintain accurate financial documentation and records. Identify financial risks and implement corrective actions. 4. Accounts Payable & Receivable Oversee vendor payments and customer billing processes. Monitor collections and outstanding receivables. Ensure accurate invoice processing and timely payments. Maintain strong vendor and customer account reconciliations. 5. Cash Flow & Financial Analysis Monitor cash balances and working capital. Manage cash flow forecasting and financial planning. Analyze operating expenses and identify cost-saving opportunities. Provide financial recommendations to executive leadership. 6. Leadership & Administration Supervise and develop accounting and finance personnel. Establish accounting procedures and departmental policies. Improve accounting processes and reporting systems. Collaborate with department managers on financial matters. Support management with special projects and financial analysis.
